name: Consent-first lead capture and journey tracker (demo)

parameters.content:
## Consent-first lead capture and journey tracker (demo)
Every request reads the whole sheet once, works out the change in **Apply the change**, and writes it back in one call.

- **Website forms**: newsletter sign-ups start *pending*; enquiries are logged with the reply basis.
- **Confirm / Unsubscribe**: the link shows a button, the button makes the change.
- **Team view**: LinkedIn CSV import, click report, unsubscribe on request, *Draft follow-ups* (Claude Haiku, to a review tab).

Edit **Settings** first. Credentials: Google Sheets OAuth2 (on both sheet nodes) and Header Auth `x-api-key` (on Claude).

### What is kept
Contacts: name, organisation, role, address, consent and activity counts. Consent log: what each form said and when. Suppression: addresses that asked to stop, so no import adds them back. Nothing is emailed: the confirm link is shown on the demo page instead. Emails and phone numbers are masked before anything reaches the AI. Demo data only (example.com addresses).

assignments.name: business_line
assignments.value: a small consultancy that helps charities and social enterprises find sponsors and partners who share their aims.

assignments.name: opt_out_line
assignments.value: Reply 'no' and I won't email again.

assignments.name: newsletter_wording
assignments.value: Yes, send me the Fernhollow Partners newsletter (about once a month). I can unsubscribe at any time from any issue.

assignments.name: enquiry_wording
assignments.value: We'll use your details to reply to your enquiry, as set out in our privacy notice.

assignments.name: linkedin_wording
assignments.value: LinkedIn form tick box: I'd like to receive the Fernhollow Partners newsletter.

assignments.name: linkedin_privacy_wording
assignments.value: LinkedIn form privacy notice: Fernhollow Partners will use these details to follow up on your request.

assignments.name: system_prompt
assignments.value:
You draft short, personal follow-up notes for {sender_name} at {business_name}, {business_line}

A person on the team reads every note before deciding whether to send it. You never send anything.

You are given facts about one contact: their first name, organisation, role, how they found us, why they are worth a personal note now, and their enquiry if they sent one.

Write the body of a note from {sender_name} that:
- Picks up the one most specific thing in the facts (their enquiry if there is one) and responds to it in plain words.
- Offers one small, easy next step: a short call, or a question they can answer by reply.
- Sounds like one person writing to another: warm, direct, British English, no sales language.
- Is 40 to 80 words, in one or two short paragraphs.

Never:
- Start with a greeting or end with a sign-off, name or opt-out line. Those are added afterwards, so don't use their first name either.
- Open with "Thanks for getting in touch" or any other stock opener. Start with the substance of what they asked.
- Include links, email addresses or phone numbers.
- State any figure, price, percentage, result or promise, or claim past work for other organisations. That includes how often you do this or how many people you have helped ("every week", "many charities").
- Mention newsletter clicks, tracking, how many times they opened anything, or that they were "scored". Say how they found us only if it reads naturally (for example "thanks for getting in touch through our website").
- Invent facts that are not in what you were given. If a fact says "(not given)", leave it out.

The subject line is under 60 characters, specific to them, and not clickbait.

Reply with JSON only: {"subject": "...", "body": "..."}

parameters.jsCode:
// One item per contact to draft for, so the Claude node runs once for each.
return $input.first().json.ai.map((a) => ({ json: a }));

// The two paths (with and without drafts) meet here, so the save and the answer are built once.
return [$input.first()];

meta.note: Demo. Fictional business and invented contacts only. Sends nothing.
